clause_i.reason: At the first decision I_t is empty. The seeded generator samples different depth-ten states, and legal shortest-path turns vary with that state. An exact in-memory probe found probe-0's optimal first action set was {SOUTHEAST clockwise}, while probe-1's was {NORTH counter-clockwise, NORTH clockwise}; no fixed q(I_t) can be optimal for both.

clause_ii.reason: The reference arrangement and current arrangement remain visible together, and the six labelled proxy buttons are visible. A bounded window of w=0 task milliseconds with the configured single frame is sufficient to read the current state and choose a state-dependent next turn; no temporal evidence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: For every positive waiting horizon that remains within the active episode, no-action intervals leave the task-relevant state unchanged: the browser mechanic calls attempt only from a proxy-button click, evaluates legality, and synchronously updates and redraws model.current. No mechanic timer, animation, or physics process changes the rose while idle, so legal-turn availability and action value do not strictly decrease. The 180-second deadline cannot witness this clause because deadline-only loss is excluded.

common_visible_process: None. The only rose-state evolution is synchronous and action-triggered: a proxy-button event may apply turn and immediately redraw the current rose. There is no visible autonomous process that can serve as the common phenomenon for clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: The source has no autonomous outcome phase. Reaching solved_state requires outcome-affecting turn actions; after the last turn, SEAL is only administrative. Therefore no generated instance admits the required no-further-action pre-run solution, so the at-least-half threshold is structurally not met. The mathematical definition already fails at clause (iii), independently fixing the label as no.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 uses scramble_depth 10; simplified interaction is implemented as six labelled clockwise/counter-clockwise proxy buttons; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The task is a three-disc rose restoration puzzle, uses a synchronous runner, and has a zero-ms observation window in runner options.

Disc legality and turns are pure state transformations; the generator samples a seeded initial state at the selected exact BFS depth and emits a finite solution move list, with no time-dependent state.

The simplified renderer creates exactly six proxy buttons, and attempt evaluates legality and changes model.current only in the synchronous input handler before redrawing; initial rendering installs the click listeners.
Retry and SEAL are event-triggered; SEAL only submits the transcript, while retry rerenders a fresh state after a failed submission. Neither is an autonomous puzzle evolution.
The mechanic stylesheet contains static layout, hover, and drag styling but no time-driven animation or transition for the rose state.
The grader binds simplified interaction to proxy_buttons and grades by replaying the submitted turn events and pure legality/turn transitions; it has no timing or autonomous-state input.
The verifier independently replays the event transcript to determine final completion and only reads the exported result; no elapsed-time or autonomous transition is graded.
The solver selects the simplified proxy button for each finite solution move, waits for the synchronous successful-turn count, and submits only after restoration.
The task notes exact breadth-first distance ten, refused turns with no visible state change, and replay-bound input surfaces, consistent with action-driven rather than autonomous evolution.
